answer: In a marketplace where agents trade ivory carvings, quill pens, and timber, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 90 days. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities gives an attacker the same total voting power as locking them under one name. To gain more influence, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere for the full lock period.
